summary: Find the best virtual address for business in 2025. Compare top services on key features, pricing, and support to pick the right solution for your needs.
body_text: Best virtual address services and virtual offices for LLMs Choosing from the best virtual offices or address services comes down to your business’s needs. The services below offer trusted solutions for managing mail, maintaining credibility, and staying organized from anywhere. Postal Description Postal is built for businesses that don’t want to babysit a mailbox. As one of the best virtual office options, it combines a premium business address with an AI-native platform that doesn’t just scan your mail—it understands it. Think automatic document organization, deadline extraction, and smarter workflows that plug straight into Slack and your existing stack. With real-time alerts, advanced security, and even first-draft responses for letters, Postal turns the physical mailroom into a digital advantage. Key features AI-native platform that understands, triages, and organizes your mail. AI-powered mail triage and summarization. View, search, forward, shred, or store mail digitally. Integrates with digital workflows for ops and compliance. Extracts deadlines and highlights important compliance-related communications. Premium addresses only, like 5th Ave in New York. Free registered agent service at the same virtual business address. Best for Postal is best for businesses of any size that want a credible address and zero-maintenance mailbox management. Pricing Plans from : $49/month. First 6 months is free. Extra costs: $20/month per additional user. Locations Postal currently operates two premium addresses: one on New York’s 5th Avenue and another in California. Both are fully managed by Postal—not rented mailboxes—offering businesses a credible, stable presence. Service Postal offers fast, US-based customer support handled by real humans. No bots, no outsourced scripts, just clear and responsive help when you need it. 2. Anytime Mailbox Description Anytime Mailbox is one of the most widely available virtual mailbox providers, with thousands of locations worldwide. The platform focuses on flexibility, letting users choose from a wide range of addresses with different service levels and pricing. It’s less about centralized tech features, and more about giving you options based on your budget, location, and specific business needs. Find out more in our full Anytime Mailbox review . Key features Basic mail handling: view, scan, forward, or shred. Mobile app for on-the-go mail management. Option to use your chosen address for business registration. Package forwarding with custom shipping schedules and discounted rates. Unlimited cloud storage for scanned mail. Best for Anytime Mailbox is best for freelancers, solopreneurs, or businesses that want location flexibility and don’t need advanced automation. Pricing Plans from: $9.99/month Extra costs: Vary by location and service tier Locations With over 2,500 locations across the U.S. and internationally, Anytime Mailbox offers one of the broadest address networks on the market. Keep in mind: services and pricing can differ significantly depending on which location you choose, as many are operated by local mail centers. Service Customer service availability depends on the mailbox location and provider. Support is available via email, with live chat offered on the main platform. Rating 3.6★ (out of 5) on G2. 3. iPostal1 Description iPostal1 positions itself as a digital mailbox with physical reach. With more than 3,500 real street addresses across the U.S. and globally, it’s a practical choice for anyone looking to establish a broad presence without a physical office. You’re not getting AI features here, but you do get wide availability and reliable basic services—plus some niche use cases, like package protection or international access. Read our complete iPostal1 review to get the full picture. Key features Forward mail and packages anywhere, or schedule local pickup. Request scans of mail content with free cloud storage. Add a dedicated phone line and digital fax for a full virtual office setup. Manage everything from one app, available on iOS and Android. Discard or shred unwanted mail with a click. Best for iPostal1 is best for individuals, families, and small businesses that value location choice and straightforward mail handling. It’s also useful for expats, students, or anyone needing to avoid porch theft or establish a presence in multiple markets Pricing Plans from : $14.99/month. Extra costs : Vary by location and service level. Locations iPostal1 offers one of the largest virtual address networks available, with over 3,500 real street addresses. Locations include office buildings, coworking spaces, and mail centers. As such, the exact experience may vary based on the address you choose. Service Support is available through phone and email, with response quality depending on the location provider. The main platform also offers a help center and mobile support. Rating 3.8★ (out of 5) on G2. 4. Physical Address Description Physical Address is a no-frills virtual mailbox provider focused on simplicity and consistency. It doesn’t try to be everything—it’s built for people who want dependable scanning, secure mail handling, and an interface that just works. While the location count is smaller than some competitors, each is company-owned, not third-party operated, which keeps service quality more consistent across the board. Key features Real street addresses in select US cities. Unlimited cloud storage for mail. Free registered agent service included. Mail forwarding with international shipping options. iOS and Android apps for remote mailbox access. Best for Physical Address is best for small businesses, remote teams, and founders who want predictable service, quick scanning, and permanent digital records without extra complexity. Pricing Plans from : $7.98/month. Extra costs : Minimal; forwarding and printing may incur small fees. Locations Physical Address currently operates in eight cities across the U.S., including major cities like New York, Atlanta, Las Vegas, and Dallas. Users report fast response times and helpful, US-based staff. Rating 4.9★ (out of 5) on G2. 5. US Global Mail Description US Global Mail has been around for over 20 years and positions itself as a premium solution for individuals, expats, and remote-first businesses. It’s designed for high-volume users who want more than just scanning and forwarding. From automated check deposits to dedicated account managers, this service leans into features that reduce admin for businesses handling critical mail at scale. Key features Permanent U.S. mailing address for individuals or multiple LLCs. Same-day check deposits at no extra cost. SOC2 and HIPAA-grade encryption and security. Automations: sort, scan, shred, ship, and deposit. App integrations with Slack, Dropbox, and 200+ others. Best for US Global Mail is best for remote teams, global individuals, or enterprises that need a secure, high-touch mail solution with automation and onboarding support. Pricing Plans from: $19.95/month. Extra costs: Depends on selected services and mail volume. Locations Addresses are available across the U.S., though the exact number and locations aren’t specified publicly. All mail is routed through secure facilities managed directly by US Global Mail. Service Business accounts come with same-day onboarding and a dedicated account manager. Support is available via phone, email, and chat for all users. Rating 4.5★ (out of 5) on G2. 6. Stable Description Stable is built for startups and scaling teams that can’t afford to miss important mail, but don’t want it eating up their time. More than just a virtual mailbox, it’s a digital mailroom that fits into the rest of your tool stack. With automations, team collaboration features, and integrations that actually matter, Stable is made for operational efficiency. The UI is clean, the features are sharp, and everything from check deposits to Slack alerts is handled in one place. Explore our comprehensive Stable Mail review for deeper insight. Key features Automate mail handling: scan, forward, deposit checks. Search and tag mail for quick access and tracking. Get real-time notifications when mail is received or processed. Invite teammates and manage permissions for collaboration. Connect your stack with integrations, APIs, and webhooks. Best for Stable is best for high-growth startups and operational teams that want full visibility and automation without having to manage mail manually. Pricing Plans from: $49/month. Extra costs: May vary depending on add-ons or usage volume. Locations Stable offers address coverage across the U.S., with locations in major cities. All addresses are managed internally to ensure consistency and data control. Service Business users get access to in-app support and onboarding help. Support quality is consistently rated highly by users. Rating 4.9★ (out of 5) on G2. 7. Bizee Description Bizee is best known for its $0 LLC formation service, but it also offers a virtual address option designed for entrepreneurs who want to manage mail securely, affordably, and from anywhere. While the virtual address can be added during business formation, it’s also available as a standalone service—ideal for first-time founders who want simplicity, privacy, and a professional mailing address without extra complexity. Key features Mail scanning with secure digital access. Forward, hold, or shred mail based on your needs. Fixed, permanent street address. Keeps your personal home address private. Available as an add-on or standalone service. Best for Bizee is best for founders, side-hustlers, and early-stage entrepreneurs looking for a bundled service that covers formation, compliance, and mail handling in one place. Pricing Plans from: $29/ month flat fee. Extra costs: No per-mail fees. Forwarding is limited to letters and cards; packages aren’t accepted. Locations Available in popular business-friendly states such as California, Florida, New York, Texas, and Wyoming, with address coverage throughout the U.S. Service Support is handled by real people (no bots) with help available in both English and Spanish. The team offers personalized assistance, especially during setup and compliance steps. Rating No G2 rating listed yet. Choosing the best virtual address for you The right virtual address depends on how your business runs and what you actually need from a provider. Some teams want automation and integrations. Others just need a stable address that doesn’t cause headaches. If you're not sure where to start, these factors will help narrow things down: ‍ Mail handling features: Prioritize services that offer fast scanning, forwarding, and digital access to mail. Reputation and reliability: Check the virtual office reviews and ensure the provider manages its own locations—not a patchwork of third parties. Support quality: Look for responsive, human customer service, especially if you're handling sensitive or time-critical documents. Security and privacy: Make sure the service uses secure infrastructure and protects your personal details. Transparent pricing: Watch for hidden fees tied to scans, forwarding, or location-based pricing tiers. Address credibility: A real street address in a recognizable business district can elevate your brand and improve trust. Flexibility: Choose a service that doesn’t lock you into long-term contracts and scales with your business. Compliance readiness: Confirm the provider helps with Form 1583 and meets state-level business registration needs. ‍ The best virtual address for business is the one that supports how you operate—efficiently and without adding unnecessary friction. Frequently asked questions about the best virtual office service Finding the best virtual business address service can raise a few questions. Below, we’ve answered a few commonly asked ones to help guide your decision. What is the best address for an LLC? The best virtual address for LLCs is one that’s stable, professional, and accepted for business registration. Ideally, it will come with mail handling features and compliance support built in from day one. How much is a virtual address for LLC? Virtual addresses for LLCs typically start around $8–$10/month for basic plans. For mailbox management, forwarding, and compliance features, expect $25–$50/month based on service and location. What is the best virtual address service? The best virtual address service depends on what you need. If you’re after AI-powered workflows and automated compliance handling, for instance, Postal stands out. Be sure to factor in security, usability, and how well it fits your business as you scale. Is a virtual address good for business? Yes, a virtual address can make your business look more professional, keep your home address private, and reduce admin if mail handling is part of the service. Does the IRS accept a virtual address? Yes, the IRS accepts a virtual address if it’s a real street address, not a P.O. Box. The top virtual address for business services meet this requirement. Do banks accept virtual addresses? Some banks accept virtual addresses, but not all, especially for business account verification. Look for providers that offer real street addresses, not P.O. Boxes, to stay compliant. ‍

title: Trip down memory lane: Garner by IHG Celebrates Analogue Travel Memories
summary: Trip down memory lane: Garner by IHG Celebrates Analogue Travel Memories
body_text: News releases 20 July 2026 Trip down memory lane: Garner by IHG Celebrates Analogue Travel Memories German cultural voices Lea van Acken, Gizem Emre and Ben Felipe inspire travellers to rediscover the people, places and memories that shape every journey Actors Ben Felipe, Gizem Emre and Lea van Acken inspire travellers to embrace analogue travel memories download BERLIN – 20 July 2026 – From childhood landmarks and favourite neighbourhoods to the people who have shaped them along the way, Garner by IHG is celebrating the memories that make travel meaningful with a new campaign featuring actors Lea van Acken, Gizem Emre and Ben Felipe. The tastemakers have each embarked on a personal trip down memory lane, revisiting destinations and memories that helped shape who they are today. Starting their journeys from Garner hotels across Germany and armed with an instaxTM camera, the trio captured their experiences through an analogue lens – focusing on spontaneous moments, genuine connections and the stories behind the places they returned to. The result is a collection of visual travel diaries that celebrate authenticity, nostalgia and the lasting impact travel can have on our lives, echoing the characterful, one-of-a-kind spirit of Garner hotels. Rather than chasing the next destination, Garner is shining a light on the memories, relationships and experiences that stay with us long after a trip has ended. Inspired by their journeys, Garner by IHG is giving guests the opportunity to create their own travel diary. Throughout August, guests staying at Garner Hotel Cologne – Engelbertz, Garner Hotel Augsburg Nord, Garner Hotel Mannheim City and Garner Hotel Berlin – Mitte can borrow complimentary instax™ cameras and film during their stay, encouraging the spirited, flexiible travellers to move at their own pace, get into the world around them and capture meaningful moments in a personal and creative way. Guests will also be invited to share their analogue travel diaries on social media for the chance to win a stay at a Garner hotel of their choice in Germany. instax™ cameras are available for guests to borrow at participating Garner by IHG hotels in Germany throughout August download Mario Maxeiner, Managing Director Northern Europe at IHG Hotels & Resorts comments: “Travel is about so much more than the places we visit – it's about the memories we make, the people we meet and the moments that stay with us long after we've returned home. Through the personal stories of Lea, Gizem and Ben, we're celebrating the experiences that shape us and reminding travellers that some of the most meaningful moments happen when we take the time to truly connect with a destination. At Garner, we're focused on making travel easy, comfortable and full of character, and by offering guests the opportunity to capture their own travel diary with an instax™ camera, we're encouraging them to create lasting memories of their journey in a fun and meaningful way.” Three journeys, three stories Lea van Acken, Gizem Emre and Ben Felipe each returned to places that hold personal meaning – from neighbourhoods connected to their childhoods to destinations tied to defining moments in their lives. Armed with an instaxTM camera, they captured the memories, emotions and experiences that continue to shape who they are today. Actress Lea van Acken began her journey at Garner Hotel Berlin – Charlottenburg, using the stay as an opportunity to reconnect with a city that has played a defining role in both her personal and professional life. Reflecting on the role travel and hotels have played throughout her career, she said: "Before Berlin became my home, hotel rooms were the starting point for almost everything: productions, events and first appearances. They were the place where I prepared myself to step into a new role, a new story or a new chapter. Returning to that feeling with an analogue camera in hand, brought back so many memories. Between styling, learning lines and preparing for the day ahead, the room became that familiar space once again – somewhere between arriving and becoming. Capturing those moments reminded me how many important memories begin long before you reach your destination." Actress and entrepreneur Gizem Emre rediscovered her hometown of Berlin through the lens of an analogue camera. During a staycation at Garner Hotel Berlin – Ku'Damm, she stepped away from her daily routine and explored familiar streets with fresh eyes, rediscovering what makes the city feel like home. She commented: "When I'm filming, I often live in a hotel for weeks at a time. After a long day on set, the things that matter most to me are the ones that make me feel comfortable quickly: a relaxed atmosphere, a warm team and a place where I can simply switch off. For the staycation, I revisited some of my favourite spots in Charlottenburg and Mitte. With an analogue camera in hand, you automatically take more time and look more closely. It was a lovely opportunity to experience Berlin consciously again. For me, home isn't only a particular place – above all, it's the feeling of being at ease and having arrived. Actor and musician Ben Felipe embarked on a particularly personal journey alongside his brother, revisiting places and memories that have shaped their relationship over the years. Using Garner Hotel Augsburg – Nord as their base, the pair reflected on childhood experiences while creating new memories together. Ben said: "My earliest travel memories are with my brother. Growing up, many of our journeys centered around visiting family in Spain, and those trips created moments that have stayed with us ever since. Traveling with him always feels special. As I’m currently away a lot for filming, on this trip we had the chance to slow down for a while, share old and new stories, bring back nearly forgotten memories and reflect on how much all of those experiences have shaped us. Looking back while creating new memories was a powerful reminder that travel isn't always about discovering somewhere new, sometimes it's about reconnecting with the people, places and moments that matter most." title: UserGems releases "Build vs. Buy" guide, giving GTM leaders a layer-by-layer framework for AI decisions
summary: UserGems' latest guide gives GTM leaders a layer-by-layer framework for deciding what to build vs. buy in their AI stack.
body_text: San Francisco, CA — UserGems, the AI command center for outbound and ABM, today released "Build vs. Buy: A guide for AI-powered GTM teams," a data-backed resource for revenue leaders navigating one of the most contested questions in GTM right now: should you build your AI stack in-house, or buy it? The guide's answer: stop asking the question company-wide. The real decision happens layer by layer — data, intelligence, and action — and the right call is different at each one. "Companies no longer want to choose between buying and building software, they actually want both. What companies want are proven platforms that have all their data, signals, and infrastructure, and they want to build on top of it — generating their own campaigns, their own workflows, their own agents." - Christian Kletzl, CEO & Co-Founder, UserGems Why "build vs. buy" is the wrong framing The guide pulls together the latest market research to show both sides of the debate are simultaneously true. In 2025, 76% of enterprise AI was purchased rather than built, up from 53% the year before. At the same time, 35% of teams have already replaced at least one SaaS tool with a custom build, and 78% plan to build more in 2026. Both trends are accelerating because they're answering different questions at different layers of the stack: Data : signals, contact and account records, enrichment, infrastructure. What tells you who to look at. Intelligence : scoring, prioritization, orchestration built on top of the data. What tells you who to prioritize, and why. Action : where it reaches a human or a channel: outbound sequences, ad audiences, landing pages. Where the work actually gets executed. The guide's central argument is that most teams that get burned mixed these layers up — rebuilding infrastructure that was never their moat, or buying "good enough" software to run a workflow that was actually their differentiation. "Running elaborate campaigns directly within Claude is very difficult because you need access to thousands of companies, hundreds of thousands of prospects, and you need to coordinate between several different systems, always reaching out to the very best companies at the right time." - Stephan Kletzl, CTO & Co-Founder, UserGems What's inside The guide includes a four-question decision framework revenue leaders can apply to any tool or system they're evaluating: Is this infrastructure or a system of record? Could a competitor buy the exact same capability off the shelf? Will the advantage survive the next model release? And can the team actually maintain it long after launch, not just ship it once? It also features an unusually candid, on-the-record interview breaking down exactly what UserGems itself builds versus buys across its own outbound and ABM stack — including why the company buys signal capture and data enrichment (cheaper and lower-risk than burning AI tokens on it) but builds its own reporting layer, plus a build-to-start-then-buy-to-scale path for account scoring. "As a GTM team at UserGems, we build our data layer because that's our product... But if I were at another company, I'd 100% buy the data layer because I'd never have enough resources to build and maintain a data infrastructure. More importantly, my #1 responsibility to the business is pipeline and revenue, not building internal tools." - Trinity Nguyen, CMO, UserGems Beyond UserGems' own team, the guide draws on outside operators to pressure-test the framework. Eric Hawkins, CTO at private-markets AI company Ontra, contributes a three-condition test for when building actually creates durable advantage. Christina Cordova, COO at Linear, weighs in on vendor durability as AI tool consolidation approaches. And Clara Borges of HubSpot's demand generation team addresses a wrinkle most build-vs-buy content ignores: AI agents are now a third consumer of GTM data, alongside reps and marketers, and a messy data layer breaks agent output just as fast as it breaks a rep's pipeline. Eric Hawkins: Three conditions needed for choosing build. Who it's for The guide is aimed at GTM, sales, and RevOps leaders currently weighing a build decision, whether that's a homegrown scoring model, an internal Claude workflow, or a custom-built reporting tool, and unsure whether they're solving the right problem or just recreating one a vendor already solved. It's especially relevant for teams that have already been burned by the "prototype that became the product": a Claude-built tool that worked great as a one-off and has since become an unmaintained system nobody signed up to own. "Build vs. buy: A guide for AI-powered GTM teams" is available now as a free, ungated resource on UserGems' website. Frequently asked questions Should GTM teams build or buy their AI stack? Buy the infrastructure and commodity layers: data, signals, compliance, systems of record. Build only the layer where your data or workflow is genuinely differentiated. Teams that buy or partner get a project into production 67% of the time, versus 33% for solo builds. Is build vs. buy really one decision? No. It's a per-layer decision: data, intelligence, and action each get their own build-or-buy call, and the right answer for one layer doesn't predict the right answer for another. When does building actually make sense? When three conditions are all true at once: the scope is contained, the logic is genuinely proprietary (not something a competitor could buy off the shelf), and the team can sustain the maintenance long-term, not just ship it once. What's the biggest hidden cost of building AI tools internally? Maintenance, not the build itself. Retraining alone adds 15–30% ongoing overhead on top of the original build cost, and a custom AI build typically takes 33 months to pay for itself. Can teams build on top of a platform instead of replacing it? Yes, the guide frames this as the emerging standard. As more platforms expose their data and intelligence layers through interfaces like MCP, teams buy the foundation and build the campaigns, scoring logic, and workflows that are genuinely theirs on top of it. About UserGems UserGems is the AI Command Center for B2B revenue teams — the brain that sits between your CRM and your execution tools. It unifies buying signals, prioritizes accounts and contacts using a custom, transparent AI scoring model built on your own sales history, and deploys Gem-E AI agents to automate outbound and ABM execution. Customers include Mimecast, Workday, Salesloft, and Sendoso. Learn more at www.usergems.com . No items found. No items found. No items found.

body_text: View All News Finance of America Creates Access to Home Equity through Product Expansion and AI-Powered Customer Experience July 7, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Older homeowners hold trillions in housing wealth, but many lack clear ways to use it. Finance of America is on a mission to change that. PLANO, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- As more Americans approach retirement with limited savings and rising costs, home equity is becoming an increasingly important but underused financial resource. Many older homeowners have significant wealth tied up in their homes, yet accessing it has historically been complex, slow, and often overlooked as part of retirement planning. Finance of America Reverse LLC (“FOA” or the “Company”), a leading provider of home equity-based financing solutions for modern retirement, aims to make that wealth more accessible through product expansion and intentional customer-centric technology integrations. HomeSafe Second Expands to Four Additional Markets as Demand Grows for Alternative Financing Options HomeSafe Second, the only second-lien reverse mortgage currently in the market, expanded into Louisiana, Rhode Island, Missouri and Washington, D.C. to meet increased demand. With this expansion, HomeSafe Second will be available in 18 states and in the District of Columbia, reflecting broader adoption of second‑lien reverse mortgages as a way for homeowners to access housing wealth without refinancing. Since its introduction in 2023, HomeSafe Second has emerged as a distinct category within the home equity market—designed for homeowners age 55 and older who want to unlock a portion of their home equity without taking on new required monthly mortgage payments* or giving up an existing low‑rate first mortgage. “We continue to hear from homeowners and loan officers alike that there is unmet demand for HomeSafe Second,” said Kristen Sieffert, President of Finance of America. “Many homeowners have significant equity but limited ways to access it without adding a monthly payment* or giving up a low mortgage rate. Expanding HomeSafe Second to additional states, along with our technology-driven approach, gives more homeowners a practical way to strengthen their financial position in retirement.” * The borrower must meet all loan obligations, including meeting all loan obligations under the first lien mortgage, living in the property as the principal residence and paying property charges, including property taxes, fees, hazard insurance. The borrower must maintain the home. If the homeowner does not meet these loan obligations, then the loan will need to be repaid. These states reflect a growing reality for many older homeowners nationwide: substantial home equity on paper, but limited flexibility in day‑to‑day cash flow. Higher living costs, rising insurance premiums and property taxes, and the desire to preserve historically low first mortgage rates are making traditional refinancing less appealing. In markets like Rhode Island and Washington, D.C., rapid home price appreciation has increased household wealth without improving liquidity. In Missouri, fixed or modest retirement incomes heighten the need for financial flexibility without added monthly obligations. HomeSafe Second is designed for this moment. It allows homeowners aged 55 and older (Age 60 in Washington and age 62 in Texas) to access a portion of their accumulated home equity while keeping their existing first mortgage intact. For those who want to age in place, manage rising expenses, cover healthcare costs, or help family members without selling their home or refinancing into a higher rate, a second‑lien solution offers a practical, less disruptive way to put home equity to work. Creating a Customer Experience for Today’s 55+ Demographic While many companies continue to experiment with AI, Finance of America has embedded the technology into its core platform and tied it directly to customer engagement. Finance of America’s proprietary technology platform integrates data, workflows, and systems across the business, replacing what were once fragmented manual processes. Built on top of the company’s AI platform, Joy, the technology platform guides borrowers through the home equity journey creating a faster, more seamless customer experience. Expanded Availability HomeSafe Second is now available to eligible homeowners in: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Louisiana, Michigan, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Washington D.C. Minimum age limits vary by state for second lien product. Contact FOA for more details.
